# @zakkster/lite-bmfont
> Zero-GC bitmap font canvas renderer. O(1) kerning via 64K Int16 LUT, multi-line alignment, zero-alloc numeric HUD output, and pre-laid-out wrapped text with H/V alignment + ellipsis.

## Install
npm i @zakkster/lite-bmfont

## Import
import { BitmapFont } from '@zakkster/lite-bmfont';

## Key Facts
- Zero GC: all state in TypedArrays, no per-frame allocation on any draw method
- Size: ~1.3 KB gzipped
- Dependencies: none
- ESM only (type: module)
- ASCII 0-255 only (Unicode intentionally excluded for performance)

## Export: VERSION (string)
Semver of this package, synced with package.json and CHANGELOG.md. Currently '2.0.1'.

## Export: BitmapFontError (class extends RangeError)
The one error the constructor throws (F-10). Extends RangeError, so a
catch (e) { if (e instanceof RangeError) } around new BitmapFont(...) still fires.
Own properties: name === 'BitmapFontError', field (the caller-facing field name,
e.g. 'chars[0].id', 'opts.checked'), value (the received value). Every message
starts 'lite-bmfont: ' and contains both.

## Export: DRAWFAST_MAX (number)
1e21 -- the largest magnitude drawFast can render. The "d.d" form of 1e21 is
exactly 24 bytes (22 integer digits + '.' + 1 decimal), the whole internal
scratch buffer. Outside [-DRAWFAST_MAX, DRAWFAST_MAX] drawFast draws nothing.
BOTH endpoints are inclusive: 1e21 renders, the next double above it does not,
so Math.max(-DRAWFAST_MAX, Math.min(DRAWFAST_MAX, v)) is always renderable.

## Export: DRAWFASTINT_MAX (number)
Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (9007199254740991, 16 digits) -- the largest magnitude
drawFastInt can render. This is the CORRECTNESS boundary, NOT the buffer boundary:
above 2^53 a double is not integer-exact and v % 10 returns noise, so drawFastInt
refuses the range instead of rendering it (contrast DRAWFAST_MAX, above which
drawFast renders the double's EXACT integer value by decimal doubling -- the two
constants answer the same principle applied to different facts). It is exact by
construction for every value it admits. The digit loop keeps its loop variables
inside Smi range (lo = n % 1e7, hi = (n - lo) / 1e7, both under 2^31), so the
BODY boxes no HeapNumber in any V8 tier -- shared with drawFast. This does not
make a >2^31 call zero-alloc: passing an argument above 2^31 (2147483648) boxes
the double at the call boundary, ~16 B/call, a caller-side cost identical before
and after this library and removable by no change to it. F-44's "boxing inside
the digit loop" was a misdiagnosis; the box is caller-side (decisions/0007).
BOTH endpoints inclusive, so
Math.max(-DRAWFASTINT_MAX, Math.min(DRAWFASTINT_MAX, v)) always renders.

## Export: GLYPH_ADVANCE_SHIFT (number)
4. The 1/16-fixed-point encoding of xadvance and kerning amount (2.0.0, 0012 fork
1, C-folded). The constructor stores Math.round(value * (1 << GLYPH_ADVANCE_SHIFT)),
i.e. value * 16, into the Int16 glyph/kerning tables, giving 1/16 px (0.0625 px)
resolution -- worst-case rounding error 0.03125 px vs v1.x's 0.5 px Int16
truncation. Exposed so a consumer reaching into `glyphs`/`kerning` decodes the
format instead of guessing 16.

## Export: GLYPH_ADVANCE_SCALE (number)
0.0625, i.e. 1 / (1 << GLYPH_ADVANCE_SHIFT). A reader recovers pixels from the
store with `stored * GLYPH_ADVANCE_SCALE`; the render bodies fold it into a
per-call constant `s16 = scale * 0.0625` (0012 fork 1). advanceOf(id) and
kernOf(a, b) apply it for you.

## Export: BitmapFont (class)

### Constructor
new BitmapFont(imageAtlas, fontJson, opts?)
  - imageAtlas: HTMLImageElement | HTMLCanvasElement. A null/undefined/primitive
    atlas throws a BitmapFontError (F-10).
  - fontJson:   standard BMFont JSON (common, chars, optional kernings). Validated
    at construction: imageAtlas, common, common.lineHeight, common.base, chars and
    (when present) kernings are checked; a malformed one throws a BitmapFontError
    naming the field -- no raw TypeError escapes. chars: [] is LEGAL (a coherent
    zero-glyph font: measure is 0, hasGlyph is false for every id).
  - opts must be a plain object or undefined/null. An unknown own key throws (F-28),
    so { missingAdvanc: 6 } -- one dropped letter -- is an error, not a silent
    default. Allowed keys:
  - opts.missingAdvance: number, default 0 (byte-identical to 1.2.x). The xadvance
    written into every glyph id the descriptor did not cover, so an absent glyph
    leaves a gap instead of overprinting the next (F-12). Must be finite in
    [0, 2047.9375] -- the 1/16 fixed-point advance range -- or the constructor
    throws. Stored as Math.round(value * 16) by the Int16 store. Id 10 is never given a missing advance.
  - opts.checked: boolean, DEFAULT TRUE (2.0.0; was false). Pass { checked: false }
    to opt out. Opens the LOSSY lane.
    Two lanes: inputs with no correct reading (a null atlas, a NaN metric, a
    non-number id, a fractional kerning key) ALWAYS throw; lossy-but-interpretable
    inputs (an atlas coord past Int16, an id outside [0, 256)) are skipped
    silently by default and throw only under checked, which reports the exact
    drift. A FRACTIONAL xadvance/amount NO LONGER throws under checked (2.0.0,
    0012 forks 1+6): 1/16 is the format's declared resolution, so a value it is
    designed to round is not lossy. Out-of-RANGE advances still throw. Storage
    CHANGED in 2.0.0: Math.round(value * 16), 1/16 fixed point.

### id-10 policy
A descriptor entry for id 10 (`\n`) is DISCARDED at construction -- width, height,
offsets, advance, and any kerning pair naming it. A newline is a layout
instruction, not a glyph. `hasGlyph(10)` is always false.

### Methods

measure(text, scale = 1) -> number
  Kerning-aware width of the WIDEST LINE of `text` at `scale`. BREAKING IN 2.0.0
  (F-06, 0012 fork 2): measure('AA\nAA') on an advance-8 font is 16; in 1.x it
  summed across newlines and returned 32. It is now an EXACT ALIAS of
  measureWidest -- same walk, same number. A newline-free string is UNCHANGED.
  There is no measureTotalAdvance: the 1.x cross-newline total had no consumer.
  Returns NaN if `text` is not a string, or if `scale` is outside (0, Infinity)
  -- NaN, 0, a negative, or Infinity (F-36). Throws after destroy().

measureWidest(text, scale = 1) -> number
  Width of the WIDEST line -- the number to size or centre a box with, and the
  one draw() aligns each line against (F-06). measureWidest('AA\nAA') is 16, and
  since 2.0.0 measure returns that same number (it delegates here). Lines split
  at \n only and the kerning chain RESETS at the break, matching draw(). A
  trailing newline yields a final empty line of width 0, so 'AAA\n' is 24.
  One pass, no split, no slice, zero allocation. CAN RETURN A NEGATIVE WIDTH: a
  negative xadvance or kerning amount is a valid Int16 the constructor accepts,
  so a line can legitimately measure negative and the result is the greatest
  (least negative) line; an empty line measures 0, which is wider than any
  negative line (F-39). Returns NaN on a non-string text or a scale outside
  (0, Infinity). Throws after destroy().

measureLine(text, start, end, scale = 1) -> number
  Width of ONE range. `start` and `end` are CLAMPED into [0, text.length] and are
  otherwise left alone -- exactly what drawWrapped does to the indices it reads
  out of a layout buffer, which is what makes this report what drawWrapped
  RENDERS instead of what a raw index walk counts. Fractional indices are read as
  charCodeAt reads them, truncated per iteration, NOT rounded at the boundary. On
  'AAAA' at advance 8: [-0.5, 2) is 16 (two glyphs, as drawn), [0.5, 2.7) is 24
  (three glyphs, as drawn), and [-Infinity, Infinity) is 32 and RETURNS
  (F-34, F-35). The clamp has the same TWO legs drawWrapped uses, so a NaN bound
  behaves as the renderer treats it: NaN start -> 0, NaN end -> text.length, so
  [0, NaN) measures the WHOLE line (F-38) -- NaN is what a Float32Array holds
  when a layout pass failed. An empty range after clamping, or a negative end,
  is 0, not NaN. Returns NaN
  on a non-string text or a scale outside (0, Infinity); door order is text,
  then scale, THEN the range, so a bad scale with an empty range is NaN, not 0.
  Throws after destroy().

### Which width do I want
  one explicit range                      -> measureLine(text, start, end, scale)
  a box that will hold every line          -> measureWidest(text, scale)
  a box that will hold every line          -> measure(text, scale) [alias, 2.0.0]

  NOTE the deliberate asymmetry: measure/measureWidest take the MAX over lines,
  but measureLine SUMS whatever is inside the explicit [start, end) range you
  hand it -- including a \n if you include one. On an advance-12 font
  measureLine('A\nA', 0, 3) is 24 while measure('A\nA') is 12. A range is the
  caller's assertion about what one line IS; drawWrapped never spans a break.

### The measure family's fail signal
NaN, across all three public faces (F-36). The renderers answer a bad `scale` by
drawing nothing; the measure family answers by returning NaN. That asymmetry is
deliberate: a renderer can decline to act, a query cannot decline to answer. The
scale door is a RANGE test -- `!(scale > 0 && scale < Infinity)` -- so 0 and -1,
which are finite, are rejected too; the text door is `typeof text === 'string'`,
not an array-like test, so a BOXED String object is rejected and returns NaN
(deliberate: the looser test admits {length: Infinity, charCodeAt(){...}}, which
never terminates). NaN is what the DOORS produce and is not unique in the
absolute -- a font with mixed-sign Int16 advances at an extreme but in-range
scale can also produce NaN or Infinity by arithmetic, unchanged from 1.3.0.

hasGlyph(id) -> boolean
  Does the descriptor cover this glyph id? Fail-closed on every non-integer: NaN,
  -1, 256, 65.5 are all false. Id 10 is always false. Throws after destroy().

advanceOf(id) -> number
  Decoded pixel advance of glyph `id` at scale 1 (2.0.0). The store holds
  Math.round(xadvance * 16) in 1/16 fixed point; this returns stored * 0.0625, so
  an xadvance 8.6 font reports advanceOf(65) === 8.625. Fail-closed: a non-integer
  or out-of-range id returns 0. Throws after destroy().

kernOf(a, b) -> number
  Decoded pixel kerning between glyphs `a` and `b` at scale 1 (2.0.0), stored * 0.0625.
  Fail-closed: a non-integer or out-of-range key returns 0. Throws after destroy().

draw(ctx, text, x, y, scale = 1, align = 0) -> void
  Multi-line `\n`-aware renderer. `align`: 0=left, 1=center, 2=right; any value
  outside {0,1,2} (NaN, negatives, fractionals) renders LEFT. A `scale` outside
  (0, Infinity) -- NaN, 0, a negative, or Infinity -- draws NOTHING and returns
  (F-11). `x`/`y` is the BASELINE anchor of the first line.
  A NON-STRING text -- null, undefined, a number, an array, a boxed String, or
  {length: Infinity, charCodeAt} -- draws NOTHING and returns (F-42, 1.4.1): the
  same `typeof text !== 'string'` door the measure family answers with NaN. Five
  text-taking faces, one door; the two text renderers draw nothing, the three measure faces return NaN;
  drawFast takes a number and has none. Detect a bad text with
  Number.isNaN(measureWidest(text)).
  PIXEL-SNAPPED PER LINE ORIGIN IN X AND PER BASELINE IN Y -- that is the exact
  scope of the promise. EVERY baseline is snapped, not just the first (F-07,
  1.4.0): line i lands at Math.round(y) + Math.round(i * lineHeight * scale).
  Glyph X is deliberately NOT snapped -- only the line origin is rounded, so at
  scale 1.1 a glyph column reads 0, 8.8, 17.6, 26.4...

drawFast(ctx, value, x, y, scale = 1, align = 0) -> void
  Zero-alloc number renderer with one decimal place (e.g. 33.4).
  - NaN / +Infinity / -Infinity -> returns silently
  - |value| > DRAWFAST_MAX (1e21) -> returns silently, draws nothing
  - Negative values inside the door -> clamped to 0 (so -5 renders "0.0")
  - Decimal rounded to the nearest tenth, EXACTLY (8.45 -> "8.4", not "8.5"):
    the tenth comes from Fast2Sum, not a value * 10 product (F-23 closed)
  - Above 2^53 (9007199254740992) every double is an integer and its digits are
    rendered EXACTLY -- the true value of the double stored, which is NOT
    necessarily the literal you typed: 762638538843020900000 renders
    "762638538843020853248.0", the double that literal became. Values outside
    [-DRAWFAST_MAX, DRAWFAST_MAX] draw nothing.
  - A `scale` outside (0, Infinity) draws NOTHING and returns (F-11), same as draw
  - Atlas must contain glyphs for '0'-'9' (48-57) and '.' (46)
  - Built for per-frame HUDs (FPS, score, timer) -- does NOT allocate a string

drawFastInt(ctx, value, x, y, scale = 1, align = 0) -> void
  Zero-alloc INTEGER renderer for COUNTS (coins, kills, score, seconds). No
  decimal point.
  - TRUNCATES toward zero: 1.9 renders "1", not "2". drawFast ROUNDS to the
    nearest tenth. Deliberate: drawFast renders a measurement, drawFastInt a
    count, and a count must never display a threshold it has not crossed.
  - Atlas must contain glyphs for '0'-'9' (48-57) ONLY -- it does NOT require the
    '.' (46) glyph drawFast requires, so a digits-only atlas can use this method.
  - Ceiling is DRAWFASTINT_MAX (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER), the CORRECTNESS boundary
    not the buffer boundary; exact by construction for every admitted value.
  - The digit loop keeps its loop variables inside Smi range (lo = n % 1e7,
    hi = (n - lo) / 1e7, both under 2^31), so the BODY boxes no HeapNumber in any
    tier. A >2^31 argument still costs ~16 B/call boxed at the CALL boundary --
    caller-side, identical before and after, removable by no library change
    (F-44 was a misdiagnosis; shared with drawFast).
  - NaN / +/-Infinity / |value| > DRAWFASTINT_MAX -> returns silently, draws nothing
  - Negative values inside the door -> clamped to 0 (so -5 renders "0")
  - A `scale` outside (0, Infinity) draws NOTHING and returns (F-11), same as draw
  - CONTRACT: ctx.drawImage MUST NOT re-enter the font. drawFast and drawFastInt
    share one 24-byte scratch buffer; a re-entrant ctx corrupts the outer call's
    digits. True for CanvasRenderingContext2D, not for an arbitrary drawImage object.

drawWrapped(ctx, text, layoutBuffer, lineCount, boxWidth, boxHeight, x, y, scale = 1, align = 0, vAlign = 0) -> void
  Renders pre-laid-out wrapped text into a bounding box, with horizontal and vertical
  alignment plus optional per-line "..." ellipsis flag. Zero-alloc -- layout is consumed
  from a caller-owned Float32Array.
  - `x`/`y` is the BOX TOP-LEFT corner (not a baseline).
  - A `scale` outside (0, Infinity) draws NOTHING and returns (F-11).
  - A NON-STRING text draws NOTHING and returns (F-42, 1.4.1), ahead of the
    buffer-length RangeError -- nothing to draw, no line count to honour.
  - `align`:  0=left,   1=center, 2=right; outside {0,1,2} renders LEFT
  - `vAlign`: 0=top,    1=middle, 2=bottom; outside {0,1,2} renders TOP
  - `layoutBuffer`: Float32Array, `lineCount * 4` floats:
        [0] startIdx   -- start char index into `text` (inclusive)
        [1] endIdx     -- end char index into `text` (exclusive)
        [2] lineWidth  - pixel width of this line AT THE RENDERED scale (used for alignment)
        [3] flags      -- 0 = normal; 1 = append "..." ellipsis after content
  - Surplus capacity in `layoutBuffer` is ignored -- reuse one buffer across renders.
  - Contract, enforced (1.2.3):
      * lineCount is floored to an integer and clamped at 0. NaN, negatives and
        values below 1 draw nothing and return (0.5 drew a full line in 1.2.2).
      * The buffer MUST hold at least lineCount*4 floats. A short buffer THROWS a
        RangeError naming both numbers (surplus lines vanished silently in 1.2.2).
      * startIdx < 0 or NaN clamps to 0; endIdx > text.length or NaN clamps to
        text.length; endIdx < startIdx draws an empty line. Fractional indices are
        truncated, not floored.
      * layoutBuffer may be any indexable with numeric length (Float64Array and a
        plain Array work identically); no type check is performed.
      * Id 10 inside a line range is NOT a line break here -- it advances 0 and
        draws nothing.
      * Pixel-snapped per LINE ORIGIN in X and per BASELINE in Y (F-07, 1.4.0).
        Line l lands at anchor + Math.round(l * lineHeight * scale), where anchor
        is the unchanged line-0 anchor Math.round(y + base * scale) plus, at
        vAlign 1/2, the separately rounded centring term. Glyph X is not snapped.
      * flags is a bitfield read via ToInt32: bit 0 (value 1) appends "...".
        (flags|0) & 1 fires, so 1.0000001 (a Float32 artifact) and -1 both draw
        the ellipsis (F-13); 2, 0 and NaN do not. A bit outside the mask throws
        under { checked: true } and is ignored otherwise.

layoutGlyphs(text, outBuffer, x, y, scale = 1, align = 0) -> number
  Lays out `text` into `outBuffer` as one stride-6 record per VISIBLE glyph and
  returns the record count. Pair with drawQuads to blit; edit dx/dy between the
  two calls to move individual glyphs (decisions/0010). Zero-alloc.
  - Record layout, stride GLYPH_STRIDE (6):
        [0] sx  -- source x in the atlas
        [1] sy  -- source y in the atlas
        [2] sw  -- UNSCALED source width  (drawQuads multiplies by its scale)
        [3] sh  -- UNSCALED source height (drawQuads multiplies by its scale)
        [4] dx  -- ABSOLUTE destination x, scale already folded in
        [5] dy  -- ABSOLUTE destination y, scale already folded in
  - Reproduces draw's arithmetic EXACTLY at the same x/y origin, scale and align:
    same per-line-origin/per-baseline Math.round snap (F-07 B1), same NaN-safe id
    gate, same gw>0 && gh>0 gate. A glyph that fails the size gate (a space)
    advances the cursor and occupies NO record.
  - `outBuffer`: Float64Array or a plain Array (NOT Float32Array -- it rounds the
    cursor and breaks round-trip identity with draw). `.length`, not byteLength,
    is checked.
  - A short buffer THROWS a plain RangeError (NOT BitmapFontError) naming the
    capacity, glyph index and need, checked per emitted record. SAFE UPPER BOUND
    is text.length * GLYPH_STRIDE -- the exact record count is NOT derivable in
    advance (spaces and out-of-range ids emit no record).
  - A NON-STRING text or a scale outside (0, Infinity) returns NaN (not 0, which
    is the honest answer for ''); nothing is written.

drawQuads(ctx, buffer, first, count, offX = 0, offY = 0, scale = 1) -> void
  Blits `count` glyph records from `buffer` starting at record `first`, one
  ctx.drawImage each. Zero-alloc.
  - offX/offY are added RAW to dx/dy -- never re-snapped (the origin round already
    happened in layoutGlyphs; decisions/0010 fork 9).
  - scale multiplies ONLY the source dims to size the destination and MUST equal
    the layout scale; dx/dy are already absolute and scaled (fork 3).
  - first/count follow drawWrapped's fork (1) idiom (fork 10): CLAMPED (NaN,
    negative or <1 count draws nothing; negative first clamps to 0; fractionals
    floored), and a range whose last record exceeds the buffer THROWS a plain
    RangeError (NOT BitmapFontError). One check per call, zero per glyph.
  - PINNED HAZARD (fork 10b): a buffer length cannot know how many records
    layoutGlyphs WROTE, so a count past the returned total but within the buffer
    draws UNWRITTEN slots. Pass drawQuads the count layoutGlyphs returned -- the
    caller's job, like drawFast's shared-scratch reentrancy hazard.

destroy() -> void
  Releases the atlas reference and typed arrays (glyphs, kerning, internal scratch).

## Export: GLYPH_STRIDE (number)
Float count per glyph record in a layoutGlyphs / drawQuads buffer:
[sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy], so 6. Size the buffer with it: the safe upper bound is
text.length * GLYPH_STRIDE.

## Export: FORMAT_VERSION (number)
The on-the-wire binary format this build reads and writes: glyph stride 7 with a
1/16-fixed-point advance in slot 6, the kerning key (first << 8) | second, the
layout-buffer 4-tuple and the quad stride 6. See FORMAT.md. Currently 2 -- the
C-folded fixed-point store (2.0.0, 0012 forks 1 and 8). Bumped only on a breaking
change to any of those. A peer that persists or exchanges these buffers pins this
constant and fails closed when it moves.

## drawWrapped layout helper (recipe)

The package does not ship a layout function -- strategy is application-specific. A minimal
greedy word-wrap fits in ~30 lines and uses the same Int16 arrays the renderer reads:

`font.glyphs` (Int16Array, stride 7) and `font.kerning` (Int16Array, 64K flat
LUT) are part of the public surface and are declared in BitmapFont.d.ts. The
stride is a cross-package contract; changing it is a major.

```js
function layoutWrap(font, text, maxWidth, out) {
    let line = 0, i = 0, len = text.length;
    while (i < len) {
        let lineStart = i, lastBreak = -1, lastBreakWidth = 0, width = 0, prevId = -1;
        while (i < len) {
            const id = text.charCodeAt(i);
            if (id === 10) break;
            if (id === 32) { lastBreak = i; lastBreakWidth = width; }
            const advance = font.advanceOf(id);          // decodes the 1/16 store
            const kern = prevId === -1 ? 0 : font.kernOf(prevId, id);
            const nextWidth = width + kern + advance;
            if (nextWidth > maxWidth && i > lineStart) {
                if (lastBreak !== -1) { i = lastBreak + 1; width = lastBreakWidth; }
                break;
            }
            width = nextWidth; prevId = id; i++;
        }
        const lineEnd = (lastBreak !== -1 && i === lastBreak + 1) ? lastBreak : i;
        const o = line * 4;
        out[o] = lineStart; out[o + 1] = lineEnd; out[o + 2] = width; out[o + 3] = 0;
        line++;
        if (i < len && text.charCodeAt(i) === 10) i++;
    }
    return line;
}

const layout = new Float32Array(64);                          // allocate once
const n = layoutWrap(font, 'Hello world...', 200, layout);
font.drawWrapped(ctx, 'Hello world...', layout, n, 200, 100, 10, 10, 1, 1, 1); // center/middle
```

## Exported types (TypeScript)
- Align       = 0 | 1 | 2
- VAlign      = 0 | 1 | 2
- BMFontJson  = { common: { lineHeight, base }, chars: BMFontChar[], kernings?: BMFontKerning[] }
- BMFontChar  = { id, x, y, width, height, xoffset, yoffset, xadvance }
- BMFontKerning = { first, second, amount }

## Subpath: @zakkster/lite-bmfont/atlas
import { generateAtlas } from '@zakkster/lite-bmfont/atlas';
A COLD, boot-time helper on its own subpath so the core imports nothing and stays
DOM-free in Node (decisions/0009). Not loaded unless asked for.

## Export: generateAtlas (function, COLD)
COLD, ALLOCATES -- the ONE allocating function in the package. Synthesizes a full
printable-ASCII mock BMFont atlas from a CSS font and returns { atlas, json }
ready for new BitmapFont(atlas, json). One canvas + one descriptor + ~95 char
entries PER CALL: a RATIFIED allocation exception (decisions/0009), called once
per theme at boot, NEVER in a frame loop, and NOT precedent for allocating
anywhere else. Signature (kept out of the method-signature column so the
docs-drift guard does not read it as a prototype method):

```
generateAtlas(size, fontCSS, fillColor, shadowColor?) -> { atlas, json }
  size        integer px in [4, 512] (feeds common.base; lower bound derived from cellH - 4 >= 1)
  fontCSS     a CSS font shorthand, e.g. "bold 36px monospace"
  fillColor   glyph fill color
  shadowColor optional drop-shadow color
```

Fails closed with AtlasError, never a bare Error/TypeError: a missing DOM
(globalThis.document.createElement), a null/unusable getContext('2d'), and a
hostile DOM whose createElement/getContext/measureText/fillText throws are all
re-thrown as AtlasError (carrying the original). A non-integer or out-of-range
size throws rather than normalizing -- size feeds common.base and { checked: true }
would reject a fractional base, so a silent snap would launder a caller bug.

## Export: AtlasError (class extends Error)
The one error generateAtlas throws. name === 'AtlasError'; own properties field
(the offending field, 'document' or 'size') and value (the received value). Every
message starts 'lite-bmfont: '.

See source file BitmapFont.js for full JSDoc API documentation.

## Testing
- Gate: `npm test` -> 0 failures. `node --expose-gc test/torture.mjs` -> prints
  exactly `ok`, exit 0. Test files: BitmapFont.test.js, boundary.test.js,
  findings.test.js (F-18 closure + the atlas extraction proofs), packaging.test.js
  (version sync + the ASCII-only Law). Torture tier T8 owns pack contents, the
  DOM-free import through the exports map, and the docs-drift guard. Counts are
  not pinned in docs -- nothing reads them, and they drifted in 1.4.0 (F-43). F-07 / F-34 / F-35 / F-36 are closed as
  real assertions; F-06 is closed (measureWidest ships and measure delegates to
  the widest-line walk); F-08's storage half is closed.
- npm run torture -> node --expose-gc test/torture.mjs: prints exactly "ok", exit 0.
  Zero-allocation is measured, not just claimed -- draw / drawFast / drawWrapped /
  measure / measureWidest / measureLine each pass maxMajor:0, maxPauseMs:4,
  maxArrayBuffersGrowth:0 and maxBytesPerCall:0 (RETAINED bytes) under
  @zakkster/lite-gc-profiler. measureWidest and measureLine additionally pass an
  allocation-VOLUME check: a retained-bytes rule cannot see transient per-call
  garbage the scavenger reclaims, so it alone would not forbid a split()-based
  implementation.
